core_obligations: Compute the two restrictions for part (1) (proof lines 16340-16354): (f^{-1}g_*F)|U_i = f_i^{-1}(g_*F|V_i) = f_i^{-1}g_{i,*}F_i, the first equality because U_i -> X -> S equals U_i -> V_i -> S and the second by the locality lemma; similarly (h_*e^{-1}F)|U_i = h_{i,*}(e^{-1}F|U_i x_X Y) = h_{i,*}e_i^{-1}F_i.

Conclude part (1) (proof lines 16355-16360): if the base change maps for the pieces are isomorphisms, then the base change map f^{-1}g_*F -> h_*e^{-1}F restricts to an isomorphism over every U_i, hence is an isomorphism because {U_i -> X} is an etale covering.

Get parts (2) and (3) (proof lines 16362-16370): repeat the argument replacing the appeal to the locality lemma by the corresponding statement for higher direct images, which covers the derived case and the abelian case degree by degree.
proof_roadmap: Restrict both sides of the base change map to the members of the covering and compute each restriction by locality.
Conclude from the covering that the global map is an isomorphism.
Repeat with the higher-direct-image locality input for the derived and degreewise abelian statements.
difficulty_reason: The lemma reduces base change statements for sheaves, for bounded complexes and for the q-th direct images to the members of an etale covering whose pieces factor through etale morphisms to the base (statement lines 16306-16337). The proof (proof lines 16339-16370) computes the restriction of both sides to each piece by locality of pushforward and pullback, concludes by the covering property, and repeats the argument with the higher-direct-image locality statement for the other two parts. H2: one locality computation applied to three statements, written out.
